entry.title: Transfer Measurement Documents Across Equipment Hierarchies in SAP PM
entry.content:
Introduction

Recently, I came across an interesting scenario related to measuring points and measurement documents. The business wanted a measurement recorded for a parent equipment to automatically be reflected on its child equipment as well. After exploring the standard functionality and going through the SAP documentation, I realized that SAP does support automatic transfer of measurement documents, but it does not create measuring points automatically. The measuring points must already exist on both the parent and child equipment.

I thought this was worth sharing because it is easy to misunderstand this functionality when working with equipment hierarchies. In this blog, I will share what I learned, explain how the standard functionality works and walk through the steps.

Example Scenario

Consider an aircraft maintenance organization where an Aircraft Engine is maintained as the parent equipment and its Accessory Gearbox is maintained as a child equipment.

  • Parent Equipment : ENG-10001
  • Child Equipment: AGB-10001

The Accessory Gearbox is mechanically driven by the aircraft engine. Every time the engine operates, the gearbox also operates. Therefore, both equipment accumulates the same operating hours. To monitor operating hours, separate measuring points are created for each equipment.

Equipment

Measuring Point

Characteristic

Aircraft Engine (ENG-10001)

  165

Engine Operating Hours

Accessory Gearbox (AGB-10001)

 167

Engine Operating Hours

Notice that both measuring points use the same measuring characteristic. After a flight, the maintenance technician records the engine operating hours.

Equipment

Measuring Point

Reading

Aircraft Engine

165

1250 Hours

This creates the original Measurement Document for the Aircraft Engine. Since a measurement document transfer relationship has already been configured between the two measuring points, SAP automatically creates another measurement document for the Accessory Gearbox with the same reading.

Prerequisites

Before testing the functionality, I ensured the following conditions were met:

  • Parent and child equipment were part of the same equipment hierarchy
  • Both equipment already had their own measuring points
  • Both measuring points used the same measuring characteristic
  • Measurement document transfer was maintained for the child measuring point

Once these prerequisites were completed, everything worked as expected.

Steps to Configure and Test

Step 1 – Create the Measuring Point for the Parent Equipment

Create a measuring point using IK01 for the parent equipment.

  • Equipment: ENG-10001
  • Characteristic: Hours

Step 2 – Create the Measuring Point for the Child Equipment

Create another measuring point for the child equipment using the same measuring characteristic.

  • Equipment: AGB-10001
  • Characteristic: Hours

This step is mandatory because SAP will not create this measuring point automatically.

Step 3 – Maintain the Transfer Relationship

Open the measuring point of the child equipment and maintain the measurement transfer relationship. This tells SAP that whenever a reading is entered on the parent measuring point, it should create a transferred measurement document for the child. Click Save once the below changes made.

Step 4 – Post a Measurement Reading

Now enter a measurement reading for the parent equipment using transaction IK11

  • Equipment: ENG-10001
  • Measuring Point: 165
  • Reading: 1250

Save the measurement document to complete the posting.

Step 5 – Check the Result

After saving, SAP automatically generates a transferred measurement document for the child equipment. The transferred document also contains reference information pointing to the original measurement document, making it easy to trace the source.

What I Learned

Initially, I expected SAP to create everything automatically once the parent measuring point was available. However, after testing and reading the SAP documentation, I found that this is not how the standard functionality works. SAP can automatically transfer measurement documents, but it cannot automatically create measuring points on child equipment. If automatic measuring point creation is required, it would need custom development using enhancements or BAdIs.

Where This Is Useful

I can see this feature being very useful in scenarios like:

  • Machines with multiple assemblies that share a common operating parameter
  • Vehicles and their components (e.g., odometer-driven maintenance on sub-assemblies)
  • Pumps and motors
  • Compressors with sub-units
  • Any equipment hierarchy where one measurement is applicable to multiple objects

Instead of entering the same reading several times, users can enter it once and SAP keeps the related equipment updated automatically.

Conclusion

This was a small but useful learning from my recent SAP PM work. If your requirement is to transfer measurement readings from a parent equipment to a child equipment, SAP standard already provides this functionality through Measurement Document Transfer. Just remember one important point, SAP automatically transfers Measurement Documents and SAP does not automatically create Measuring Points. Understanding this difference can save a lot of time during implementation and help set the right expectations with the business. I hope this helps other SAP PM consultants who run into similar requirements while working with equipment hierarchies.

Quick Reference

T-Code

Purpose

IK01

Create a measuring point

IK02

Change a measuring point 

IK03

Display a measuring point

IK11

Enter a measurement/counter reading

IK17

Display measurement documents

entry.title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2607
entry.content:
In this month's update, SAP Asset Performance Management 2607 brings improvements that make it easier to navigate between systems, standardise how consequence risk is evaluated, and get help without ever leaving the application. If you're looking for better integration with SAP S/4HANA, more consistent risk assessment templates, or faster access to support, this release has something for you!

Before we start, register for the upcoming webcast "What's New in APM 2608" here. If you're not subscribed to the SAP Intelligent Asset Management Community Engagement newsletter, you can register here. This will keep you up to date on upcoming What's New, Roadmap and Expert webcasts.

Now, let's take a closer look at SAP Asset Performance Management 2607.

Asset Data and Information Management

Navigate Directly to Technical Objects in SAP S/4HANA

What if you could jump from an asset record in SAP APM straight to its full technical object detail in SAP S/4HANA *? Without switching applications and without extra steps...

With this release, we've introduced a direct navigation button on the Technical Object details page, so reliability engineers can move seamlessly between APM and SAP S/4HANA in a single click.

Challenge

For customers running SAP APM alongside SAP S/4HANA, the technical object record in S/4HANA often holds information that reliability engineers need as part of their day-to-day work - full asset history, hierarchy views, and additional attributes maintained in ERP.

Until now, accessing that information meant leaving APM, opening S/4HANA separately, and locating the same object manually. For teams working across large asset bases, this context-switching added friction to every investigation and lookup.

Solution

A new navigation button appears directly on the Technical Object details page in SAP APM. *For customers running S/4HANA 2020 or above (cloud public and private), the button opens the corresponding technical object record in S/4HANA in a new browser tab -using the existing integration and authorization framework with no additional configuration required.

Navigate directly from SAP APM to the corresponding technical object in SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud.

Key details:

  • No additional access permissions needed — the button respects existing object-level authorizations automatically
  • Available across both sIoT and eIoT deployment models for consistent behavior regardless of landscape setup
  • Automatically hidden for SAP ERP ECC and S/4HANA releases below the supported version, so users only see options relevant to their system

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Fewer application switches per object lookup
  • Faster access to complete technical object detail in S/4HANA

No extra setup or access configuration required.

For more information, see Viewing Data Related to a Specific Technical Object.

 

Asset Risk Assessment

Manage Templates for Consequence Assessments

What if every reliability engineer in your organisation worked from the same consequence evaluation framework, with consistent scoring, colour coding, and full auditability? 

With this release, we have introduced a dedicated application (Manage Templates for Consequence Assessments) to create, configure, and govern consequence assessment templates, giving teams a standardised foundation for risk evaluation across sites and regions.

This is also the first step in a broader story. Until now, reliability assessments in SAP APM - FMEA, RCM, risk and criticality - applied to individual technical objects. With this release, we are beginning to bring assessment capabilities to industrial system objects as well. Consequence assessment templates are the foundation - the actual consequence assessments on industrial systems will follow later in 2026.

New application "Manage Templates for Consequence Assessments" on the APM SAP Fiori Launchpad

Challenge

Consequence assessment setup was handled differently across teams, with localised configurations, inconsistent scoring scales, and no controlled way to update them without disrupting assessments already in progress. There was no single, reusable standard that reliability engineers could build on.

Solution

The new Manage Templates for Consequence Assessments application lets administrators define exactly how consequence evaluations are structured and scored. For each template, you configure the impacts to assess, a scoring formula, and colour-coded severity thresholds. Once released, a template is locked and versioned, ensuring that every assessment reflects the framework against which it was conducted.

Threshold configuration screen showing three colour-coded severity ranges — green (low), yellow (medium), and red (high) — for a consequence assessment template in SAP Asset Performance Management.

Key Details

  • Define up to 30 impacts with custom dimensions and scoring scales.
  • Build a calculation formula using arithmetic operators, aggregate functions, and fixed weights.
  • Set up to 10 colour-coded severity thresholds with custom labels.
  • Govern templates through a full lifecycle: create, release, reopen, and version them without disrupting assessments already in progress.
  • Copy an existing template to create a variation for a different site or region.

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Standardised, auditable consequence assessments across the organisation
  • Faster assessment setup with reusable, governed templates
  • Colour-coded severity scores for clear communication with stakeholders

For more information, see Manage Templates for Consequence Assessments.

Track When Risk Assessments Were Released

Knowing when a risk assessment was completed matters - for compliance reporting, maintenance planning, and understanding how your risk posture has evolved over time.

With this release, a new Released On date field is now captured at the assessment level in SAP APM. The field is set automatically when an assessment is released and is available as a filter in the assessment list and in the Analytics application for date-based reporting. Historical assessments are migrated automatically, so existing data is consistent from day one.

Key details:

  • Released On date is set automatically — no manual entry needed
  • Available as a filter in the assessment list view
  • Surfaces in Analytics for date-range reporting — by year, quarter, or specific milestone

For more information, see the SAP Help Portal:

  • Manage Risk and Criticality Assessments

SAP Built-In Support Now Available in APM

What if you could search for help, find relevant documentation, and raise a support ticket, all without leaving the application you are working in?

With this release, SAP Asset Performance Management now includes SAP Built-In Support directly in the Fiori Launchpad.

Challenge

When users ran into an issue or had a question, the only option was to leave APM, open a separate support channel, and try to describe the context from memory. For teams working across complex asset portfolios, this friction added up and meant support tickets often lacked the detail needed to resolve them quickly.

Solution

A new support panel is now available directly within SAP APM. Choose the help icon at the top right of any app or the Fiori Launchpad to access it. From there, you can search SAP Support content and SAP Community without switching tools, get recommended documentation based on the page you are currently on, and create a ServiceNow incident with the correct ACH component suggested automatically.

Access SAP Built-In Support directly from the SAP APM Fiori Launchpad for context-aware help and support content.

Key details:

  • Context-aware help, with recommended documentation linked to the page you are currently on
  • Search across SAP Support and SAP Community without leaving APM
  • Raise a support incident with the correct component pre-filled, with no more guessing

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Fewer application switches when troubleshooting or seeking guidance
  • Support tickets raised with the correct ACH component, reducing routing errors
  • Faster time to resolution for end-user queries

For more information, see Getting Support.

entry.title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2608
entry.content:
SAP Asset Performance Management 2608 is a release about reducing friction - the kind that builds up quietly over time and slows down the work that matters. Rules that had to be manually recreated in every tenant. Recommendations that took too many clicks to action. Assessments that were hard to revisit as conditions changed. Guidance that lived outside the product when users needed it most. Template and library versions that changed silently, leaving engineers working with outdated configurations without realising it. This release addresses each of those pain points directly, with changes that reliability engineers and maintenance planners will notice from day one.

Before we start, I'd like to mention a few interesting things:

  • Join us for the live webcast What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2608 on Tuesday, 8 September 2026 at 4:00 PM CEST. You can ask us questions live in the chat. Register here.
  • SAP partners can also look forward to the Product Expert Training (PET) H2 2026 series, running 28 September to 16 October. The SAP Asset Performance Management session takes place on 13 October, 11:30-12:15 CET. An active SAP Learning Hub license is required - find more information about registration for the onsite or online sessions here.
  • We've also updated our ongoing innovation overview (formerly Stay Current), a curated guide to recent SAP APM innovations. It combines feature one-pagers with direct links to supporting enablement materials, including Help Portal documentation, videos, blogs, and other useful resources. The latest edition now covers releases 2509-2608. View or download it here.

Now, let's take a closer look at SAP APM 2608.

Asset Data and Information Management

 

Stay Informed When Reference Designator Libraries or System Template Versions Become Obsolete

What if engineers were proactively informed the moment a Reference Designator Library or Industrial System Template version they are using is superseded - with a clear view of what has changed and what it means for their systems?

With this release, SAP APM actively surfaces obsolescence information for RDS library versions and Industrial System Template versions so engineers always know when a configuration they rely on has been updated.

Challenge

When a Reference Designator (RDS) Library or Industrial System Template version is superseded and marked obsolete, engineers had no visibility into the change or its impact on systems already in use. There was no notification, no warning on affected assessments, and no way to tell at a glance whether the configuration in use was still current. Engineers were left working with outdated configurations without realising it - a risk that compounds over time as libraries and templates continue to evolve.

Solution

SAP APM now actively informs engineers when versions they are using have been superseded. When an RDS library version linked to an Industrial System Instance is marked obsolete with a new version released, an information message is displayed with delta changes highlighted - so engineers can immediately evaluate whether to adopt the new version. When an Industrial System Template version is superseded, the obsolescence is reflected directly on the associated Industrial System Instance.

Assessments also surface obsolete system version indicators alongside system element details, ensuring engineers have the full context needed to decide whether to update or continue with the current version. The information is visible where it is needed - in the system instance and in the assessment - without requiring engineers to track version currency manually.

Key Details

  • Information message displayed on Industrial System Instances when a linked RDS library version is marked obsolete and a newer version is available
  • Delta changes highlighted so engineers can evaluate the impact before deciding to update
  • Obsolete Industrial System Template versions reflected on associated Industrial System Instances
  • Assessments surface obsolete system version indicators alongside system element details

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • No more silent version drift - engineers are proactively informed when configurations they rely on become obsolete
  • Delta change visibility reduces the effort of evaluating whether to adopt a new version
  • Assessments reflect current version status, supporting accurate and up-to-date risk and reliability analysis

Watch the demo:

Watch the demo: Managing Reference Designator Library Updates in Industrial Systems | SAP Asset Performance Management

For more information, see the SAP Help Portal  .

Asset Reliability Engineering

Reassess RCM Assessments

What if revisiting a released RCM assessment was as straightforward as starting a new one - with all the history preserved and all the valid work carried forward automatically?

With this release, a formal reassessment process is now available for Reliability-Centred Maintenance assessments in SAP APM.

Challenge

Reliability-Centred Maintenance assessments are not a one-time exercise. Asset conditions change, new failures emerge in the field, and validity periods expire - but until now there was no formal way to update a released assessment while preserving its history.

Solution

A new Reassess action creates a new editable version of the assessment, carrying forward all valid content automatically. A summary dialogue flags anything that needs attention before proceeding, and the previous version remains active until the new one is released.

A released RCM assessment record with the "Reassess" button highlighted

This gives customers:

  • Continuous lifecycle management - assessments stay current as conditions evolve
  • Full audit trail across versions with automatic version transitions
  • Valid recommendations carry forward automatically - no manual rebuilding

For full details, see Reassessing an Assessment on the SAP Help Portal.

Bulk Assign Task Lists to Multiple Recommendations Simultaneously

What if assigning the same task list to dozens of recommendations after an RCM or FMEA analysis took a single action instead of many repetitive clicks?

With this release, maintenance planners can now assign task lists to multiple recommendations at once directly from the Implement Recommendations list page.

Challenge

After an RCM or FMEA analysis, assigning task lists meant opening each recommendation individually and repeating the same steps every time - a pain point flagged directly by customers.

Solution

A new bulk Assign Task List action lets planners select multiple recommendations and assign one or more task lists to all of them in a single operation. Delta logic skips any task lists already assigned, so duplicates are never created.

Three RCM recommendations in "Implementation in Process" status selected simultaneously, with the "Assign Task Lists" button highlighted to assign task lists to all of them in one action.

This gives customers:

  • Significantly less manual effort after RCM or FMEA analysis
  • No duplicate assignments - delta logic handles existing assignments automatically
  • Clear feedback on every bulk operation

Watch this demo:

Watch the demo: 2608 Bulk Assign Tasklists to Recommendations - SAP Asset Performance Management

For full details, see Assigning Task Lists to Multiple Recommendations on the SAP Help Portal.

Extended Consolidation Support for Recommendations

What if you could consolidate recommendations regardless of whether they have maintenance data attached, come from different sources, or sit at different version numbers?

With this release, the recommendation consolidation capability introduced in 2604 is significantly extended to cover a much broader range of real-world recommendation sets.

Challenge

Until. now, recommendation consolidation worked under a narrow set of conditions. Recommendations with maintenance plans, task lists, or rules attached could not be consolidated. Neither could recommendations from different assessment sources, or those at different version numbers. For teams managing large and complex recommendation backlogs, these restrictions meant the feature was rarely usable in practice.

Solution

Two hard restrictions from the original 2604 implementation are now removed. Recommendations containing maintenance plans, task lists, or rules can now be consolidated - if maintenance data is present, it is automatically reassigned from the source recommendation to the new consolidated recommendation. Also, assessment-based recommendations can now be consolidated together with standalone recommendations, with the assessment-based recommendation always taking the leading role.

Version management during consolidation is also handled automatically. When reassessed recommendations are consolidated, the selected version transitions to Consolidated and the previous version is set to Obsolete - keeping recommendation history clean without manual intervention.

A "Consolidated Recommendation Details" dialog showing the resulting consolidated recommendation and its 2 source recommendations, with a warning that existing maintenance data will be relinked,This gives customers:

  • Broader consolidation coverage across recommendation types and versions
  • Fewer open duplicate or overlapping recommendations
  • Version history stays clean automatically

For full details, see Consolidating Recommendations on the SAP Help Portal.

Asset Health Monitoring

Transport Rules Across Tenants*

What if the rules you validated in your quality system could be moved to production in a single operation - with no manual recreation and no risk of configuration drift?

With this release, SAP APM introduces a transport mechanism to move rules and data sets directly between tenants. (*This feature is currently available with Early Adopter Access)

Challenge

Rules built and validated in a quality or development tenant had to be recreated by hand in production - introducing the risk of configuration mistakes and rule logic drifting between environments.

Solution

A new transport mechanism allows rules and data sets to be exported from one tenant and imported into another, ensuring identical rule logic across all tenants after a single validation cycle.

A list of RCM monitoring rules with the "Transport" button highlighted, allowing selected rules to be transported across system landscapes.

This gives customers:

  • Rapid rollout of validated rules after a single quality check
  • Consistent rule logic across all environments
  • Fewer configuration mistakes by eliminating manual recreation

Watch the following demo

Watch the demo: 2608 Transport of Rules Between Tenants EAC - SAP Asset Performance Management

For information about early adopter access, refer to Getting Early Adopter Access to New Features and Functions.

General

Product Guidance Videos Now Available in SAP Companion

What if the video guidance you needed was right there in the product - relevant to the screen you are on, without opening a browser tab or searching YouTube?

With this release, task-focused guidance videos are now available directly inside SAP Companion, the in-app help panel in SAP APM.

Challenge

When users needed help, they could not find video help directly in the application, instead having to search externally for help.

Solution

Guidance videos (where available) are now embedded in SAP Companion, context-aware to the screen you are on. Videos are organised by business capability and coverage will expand with every release.

SAP Companion showing contextual help for "Manage Reliability Cases" with an embedded demo video, highlighted alongside its matching help topic entry in the side panel.

This gives customers:

  • Task-focused video guidance without leaving SAP APM
  • Context-aware help surfaced to the screen they are on
  • Expanding coverage with every release

For full details, see SAP APM Playlists by Business Capability on the SAP Help Portal.

entry.title: Configuring and Navigating Object Links in SAP EAM
entry.content:
Deep Dive: Configuring and Navigating Object Links in SAP EAM (A Practitioner's Guide)

Introduction

If you have ever spent hours navigating across IE03 (Display Equipment), IW23 (Display Notification), and CV03N (Display Document) just to understand why a critical asset failed, you know the pain of fragmented data. While standard SAP object relationships (like an Equipment linked to a Maintenance Order) exist out of the box, true Object Links in SAP Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)—specifically connecting Technical Objects directly to Document Management System (DMS) records or linking equipment-to-equipment networks—require deliberate configuration and project-level execution.

In this guide, I will share how we configured and deployed Object Links during an S/4HANA EAM rollout, including the exact transaction codes, SPRO configuration steps, a real troubleshooting scenario, and screen navigation paths.

The Business Scenario: Overhauling a Centrifugal Pump

On a recent plant maintenance project, our maintenance technicians needed immediate access to technical drawings, vendor manuals, and inspection reports directly from the Equipment Master (IE01 / IE02) and Functional Location Master (IL01 / IL02).

Without Object Links configured between DMS document Info Records (DIRs) and Technical Objects, technicians were constantly searching external file servers or manually searching CV04N.

We implemented direct Object Linking in SAP DMS (CV01N) to link Document Types directly to Equipment (EQUI) and Functional Locations (IFLOT).

Step-by-Step Configuration Path (SPRO)

To make Object Links functional for Technical Objects, you must enable the specific SAP object table inside DMS configuration.

Step 1: Define Object Linkable Objects in DMS

  1. Go to transaction SPRO.
  2. Navigate to: Cross-Application Components → Document Management → Control Data → Define Document Types.
  3. Select your Document Type (e.g., ZMAN for Vendor Manuals or ZDWG for Engineering Drawings).
  4. Double-click Define Object Links.
  5. Add the relevant SAP Database Tables:
    • EQUI (Equipment)
    • IFLOT (Functional Location)
    • PMRIN (Maintenance Notification)
    • AUFK (Maintenance Order)
  6. Assign the Screen Number (Standard SAP screen for Equipment Object Links is 241 / Functional Location is 242).
SPRO Path:
Cross-Application Components
 └── Document Management
      └── Control Data
           └── Define Document Types
                └── [Select Doc Type] --> Define Object Links
                     ├── Table: EQUI  | Screen: 241
                     └── Table: IFLOT | Screen: 242

Master Data Maintenance: Linking Objects in Action

Once configuration is live, here is how we create and navigate the link in daily operations:

1. Linking a Document to Equipment (CV01N / IE02)

  • Go to CV01N to create a Document Info Record (DIR).
  • On the Object Links tab, select the Equipment sub-tab.
  • Enter the Equipment Number (e.g., 10004581 for the Centrifugal Pump).
  • Attach the original PDF (e.g., Pump_O&M_Manual.pdf) via the KPro storage category.
  • Save the DIR.

2. Navigating from Equipment Master (IE03)

  • Open IE03 for Equipment 10004581.
  • Navigate to the Environment → Document Link menu (or click the Document Assignment button on the screen header).
  • The SAP system displays all attached DIRs directly linked to this specific pump instance.

Real Project Troubleshooting: The Missing Link Screen

During user acceptance testing (UAT), technicians reported that while they could attach documents in CV01N, they could not view or add document links directly inside the Equipment Master (IE02) under the Document tab.

The Root Cause:
  1. View Profile Configuration: The Equipment Category (M - Machines) did not have the Document Link subscreen assigned in its View Profile.
  2. Missing Authorizations: Users were missing authorization object C_DRAW_TCD for activity 02 (Change) on the specific Document Type.

How We Resolved It:

  • Go to SPRO → Plant Maintenance and Customer Service → Master Data in Plant Maintenance and Customer Service → Technical Objects → Equipment → Equipment Categories → Maintain Picture Sequence for Equipment Categories.
  • Select Equipment Category M.
  • Add the subscreen 120 (Documents) to the screen sequence profile.
  • Updated the security role with C_DRAW_TCD activity 02.

After transports were pushed, the Documents tab appeared inside IE02 / IE03, allowing seamless two-way navigation between the technical object and DMS records.

Architectural Distinctions: Object Link vs. GOS Attachment

A common point of confusion during implementation is choosing between Generic Object Services (GOS) and SAP DMS Object Links. Here is how we evaluate them on implementation projects:

Feature GOS (Generic Object Services) SAP DMS Object Links (CV01N)

Primary UseQuick, ad-hoc file attachments (e.g., photo of a broken seal)Structured, controlled technical documentation
Version ControlNo versioning supportFull revision & version management (CV02N)
Status ManagementNo approval workflowsStatus network (Draft → Released → Archived)
SearchabilityHard to search globally across assetsSearchable via classification & metadata (CV04N)
T-Code AccessAccessible via top-left title bar iconManaged via CV01N / CV02N / IE02 / IH01

Navigating the Asset Structure via Structural Display (IH01)

To view connected object relationships across an entire plant hierarchy, we rely on IH01 (Functional Location Structure) or IH08 (Equipment Display).

  1. Execute IH01.
  2. Enter the Top-Level Functional Location (e.g., PLANT1-PUMP-AREA).
  3. Expand the structure tree to view installed Equipment, active Maintenance Notifications (IW21 / IW23 / IW28), and attached DMS documents.
  4. Double-click any linked line item to branch directly into CV03N or IW33.

This multi-level object visibility ensures that a reliability engineer evaluating repeated pump vibrations can trace from the Functional Location → Equipment → Notifications → Orders → Installed Components → Original OEM Drawings in a single session.

Conclusion

Setting up Object Links in SAP EAM goes beyond standard system usage—it bridges technical data gaps across maintenance operations, engineering, and document control. By properly mapping table links in SPRO for DMS and configuring Equipment view profiles, you transform static master data into an interconnected maintenance hub.

entry.title: Service Procurement Using Maintenance Plan in SAP PM
entry.content:
INTRODUCTION

In one of my recent SAP PM projects at a manufacturing plant, we had a recurring requirement that was a good fit for Service Procurement using a Maintenance Plan I would like to share the steps we followed.

For example, let’s take a plant which have about 40 elevators and 15 air conditioning units across different buildings. All of these were under Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) with external vendors. Every month, the vendor would come and do preventive maintenance, and the plant would get an invoice. The ask was to automatically plan these external services. The solution was to use Maintenance plan for Service Procurement.

STEP BY STEP PROCESS FLOW

Step: 1 Create a Purchase Contract using ME31K. Maintain the Agreement type, supplier, Purchasing Organization and Purchasing group. Maintain it as Service(D) and Account assignment as F.

Step: 2 Create a Maintenance Order in IW31. Enter the required technical object and maintain the Control Key as PM03 for external service. In the Agreement field, enter the Purchase Contract created in Step-1 Release the order and Save.

Step 3 Once the order is Released, a Purchase Requisition (PR) is generated automatically. Create a Purchase Order in ME21N by using this PR

Step 4 Create a Maintenance Plan in IP01 using the Maintenance Plan Category MM Service Procurement. Enter the Cycle, Unit and Purchase Order created

Step 5 Schedule the Maintenance Plan in IP10. Click Start to schedule the plan and Save it

Once the plan is Scheduled, Select the line item and click on the display object.  A Periodic Service entry sheet will be created automatically.

In our case, the Service Entry Sheet (SES) was automatically created by the Maintenance Plan. The only remaining step was to accept the Service Entry Sheet.

CONCLUSION

By using a Maintenance Plan for Service Procurement, we were able to plan recurring external maintenance services in a structured and automated manner. The process connected the maintenance and procurement activities, from the Purchase Contract and Maintenance Order through to the Purchase Order and Service Entry Sheet. This helped us plan the recurring external maintenance services through the Maintenance Plan and reduce the manual effort involved in creating service-related documents for the planned month.

entry.title: Bulk upload of HRMS-Assignment in SAP PM Work Center
entry.content:
Introduction

While working in one of Project, there was a requirement to assign multiple HR persons to a work center. When the number of assignments is small, these can be maintained manually. However, when there are many work centers and multiple persons to be assigned to each work center, performing the activity manually can be time-consuming. In this scenario, LSMW  can be used to automate the assignment.

In this blog, I will explain one approach to handle the LSMW recording when the same field name, `SHORT`, is used for both the HR work center object abbreviation and the persons being assigned.

The requirement was to assign multiple HR persons to a PM work center using LSMW. During the batch input recording, I noticed that the field name `SHORT` was used for both

- The HR work center/object abbreviation.
- The persons that need to be assigned to the work center.

As the same field name was appearing multiple times, it was needed to differentiate the fields in the LSMW source structure.

LSMW Recording

Create a LSMW and do the recording. After Batch input recording, make as default all. The first field name `SHORT` represented the HR work center/object abbreviation, while the subsequent `SHORT` fields represented the persons to be assigned. As the same field name was generated multiple times, I changed the names of the fields corresponding to the persons.

For the persons to be assigned, I changed the field names as SHORT_1, SHORT_2, SHORT_3 and so on based on the number of persons to be uploaded

After defining the source fields, the corresponding fields can be mapped to the recorded fields in the LSMW field mapping step. This allows the same `SHORT` field from the recording to be handled as separate source fields in LSMW.

Based on the above structure, the source file can contain the work center and the persons to be assigned,

Execute the LSMW steps. Once the mapping and conversion rules are completed, the normal LSMW processing steps can be followed:

Mapping:

Once the source fields are defined auto field mapping is done, it gets automatically mapped to the edited source fields

1. Read Data

This step reads the legacy/source data from an external file, such as a CSV, TXT, or tab-delimited file, into LSMW. This step allows to check the data that LSMW has read from the source file.

2. Display Read Data

This step allows to check the data that LSMW has read from the source file.

3. Convert Data

In this step, LSMW converts the source data into the format required by SAP and this is where the field mapping and conversion rules defined earlier are applied.

4. Display Converted Data

This step allows to check the converted data before creating the batch input session.

5. Create Batch Input Session

Once the converted data looks correct, LSMW creates a Batch Input Session and the session contains the data that will be processed through the SAP transaction.

6. Process the Batch Input Session

Finally, the batch input session is processed, SAP executes the relevant transaction using the data stored in the session.

After processing the session, the HR persons should be assigned to the respective PM work centers. The main challenge in this scenario was that `SHORT` was used for different purposes in the batch input recording.

Conclusion

LSMW can be useful for mass assignments in SAP PM, especially when the same activity needs to be repeated for a large number of work centers. In this case, renaming the duplicate 'SHORT' fields after using Default All provided a simple way to distinguish the work center object abbreviation from the multiple HR persons being assigned.

entry.title: SAP Asset Performance Management Reliability Cases: A Practical Walkthrough Of Root Cause Analysis
entry.content:
This blog outlines how SAP Asset Performance Management Reliability Cases can be used to investigate asset health alerts using a structured 5 Why Root Cause Analysis approach.

While condition monitoring and threshold-based alerts help organizations detect abnormal conditions early, Identifying an issue is only the first step. Maintenance and Reliability teams must also determine why the condition occurred, eliminate the root cause, and prevent the recurrence.

Why Reliability Cases Matter?

Many Organizations use condition monitoring and predictive maintenance techniques to identify abnormal asset behavior. However detecting that abnormal behavior does not explain:

  • Why did it occur?
  • What Caused It?
  • How can it be prevented from happening again?

This is where the Reliability Cases become valuable. A reliability case is created to capture and investigate failures or functional disruptions affecting industrial assets. Once the initial failure event has been recorded, a deeper investigation is often required to understand not just what went wrong, but why. Reliability Cases provide a structured approach for "Root Cause Analysis" with Failure Mode Assignment and Action Tracking.

Business Use Case:

I have selected one of the main power transformers in the plant Sub-Station area, i.e., 132/33KV, 50 MVA Power Transformer (Equipment ID:10001789), which supplies power to plant operations. The Transformer is monitored using Indicators:

SAP Asset Performance Management (APM) continuously evaluates incoming operational data for the indicators and compares it against defined alerts rules. Based on the operational data that has been received by SAP APM, the system has triggered an alert for the Indicator "Oil Temperature Rise". 

At this stage , SAP APM has just identified the abnormality but not the cause.

Now let us create a "Reliability Case" and perform "Root Cause Analysis". Each "Root Cause Analysis" progresses through the following statuses: Created --> In Process --> Completed.

Reliability Case: 

Let us create a reliability case:

let us now assign the alert and technical Object.

Let us now perform the "Root Cause Analysis".

The root cause analysis provides deeper layer of investigation and it is initiated within the reliability case to systematically trace chain of causation back to its origin, identifying the underlying condition that triggered the failure in the first place.

Let us now use 5 Why methodology and build a structured cause chain starting from the problem statement and progressively asking "Why did this occur?" at each level until the root cause is identified. Based on the findings, one or more follow-up actions can be defined within the analysis as corrective or Improvement or preventive measures.

Let us create "Why 1":

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 1".

 

Let us create "Why 2":

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 2".

 

Let us create "Why 3":

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 3"

 

Let us create "Why 4".

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 4"

 

Let us create "Why 5":

At this point, the investigation has revealed two contributing causes. So, let us expand and create two branches for this "Why" chain. One is focusing on the physical asset failure and the other one is on the maintenance process gap. Let us also attach corrective and preventive action nodes to each branch node.

Branch-1:

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 5 : Branch -1"

 

Branch-2:

Let us assign "Failure Modes" and "Causes" to "Why 5 : Branch -2".

Let us now create action nodes for these two branches.

Action Node for Branch-1: Replace tank cover gasket and inspect all transformer sealing points.

Action Node for Branch-2: Enhance preventive maintenance strategy and implement condition-based monitoring.

Mini Note: We can add multiple action nodes to a single "Why" node if needed.

Let us add one more action node for Branch-2: Since the oil is contaminated, restore the transformer oil to approved level.

5 Why Analysis:

After Identifying the systematic root cause in the 5 Why branch, the next step is to establish and link mitigation actions. In SAP APM, existing "Reliability Case Action Items" can be associated with Root Cause Analysis action nodes to ensure that root cause findings are translated into executable corrective or improvement or preventive measures.

We can now change the status of the "Root Cause Analysis" to "In Process".

 

Let us now create "Reliability Case Action Items" and assign them to "Action Nodes" of  "Why 5" branch.

In our case, I have created three "Reliability Case Action Items":

We can add a "Note" to the "Reliability Case Action Item: OTH-11":

Once we have created the "Reliability Case Action Items", we can add them to "Action Nodes" of "Why 5".

 Let us now change the status of the "Reliability Case" to "In Process".

Mini Note: The status transition to "In Process" is a critical step in Reliability Case life cycle. Before changing the status, the investigation scope , problem statement, and initial Why Why analysis should be reviewed and validated. Once the status of the "Root Cause Analysis" , the "Reliability Case", and the "Reliability Case Action Item" is changed to "In Process", the system does not allow the deletion of the "Root Cause Analysis" , the "Reliability Case", and the "Reliability Case Action Items".

Once we add all the "Reliability Case Action Items" to the "Why 5" action nodes, we can execute the required corrective or improvement or preventive actions.

Since the "Root Cause Analysis" has been completed, let us change the status of the "Root Cause Analysis" to "Completed".

Root Cause Analysis status changed to "Completed"

And release the "Reliability Case Action Items" for the execution.

Reliability Case Action Items status changed to "Released"

A "Reliability Case" itself does not execute the work. It defines the root cause and links the required actions. The actions can be executed through Maintenance Notifications and Maintenance Orders.

In this scenario, SAP APM rule has generated a Maintenance Notification when the measurement reading exceeded the predefined threshold values of "Top Oil Temperature Rise" Indicator. We can use the same Maintenance Notification for planning , execution and tracking maintenance actions arising from the "Reliability Case".

Let us create a Maintenance Order for the Maintenance Notification.

 

The Maintenance Order was successfully executed and all associated "Reliability Case Action Items" were completed. With the successful completion of "Reliability Case Action Items", the identified physical root cause was eliminated, and the systematic gaps were addressed. Therefore, the "Reliability Case" can now be formally closed.

Key Business Benefits:

  • Establish a structured root cause analysis process.
  • Ensure Corrective or Improvement or Preventive actions are formally tracked and verified.
  • Preserve organizational knowledge through documented investigations.
  • Transform alerts into structured actionable Investigations.
  • Maintain traceability from alert detection through case closure.
  • Support data driven reliability centered maintenance practices.

entry.title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2609
entry.content:
SAP Asset Performance Management 2609 includes a feature you've been asking me about for a long time - a structured 5 Whys root cause analysis built directly into Reliability Cases. No more switching to a spreadsheet or whiteboard mid-investigation. This release also brings improvements in IoT-driven condition monitoring.

Before we start, I'd like to mention a couple of enablement materials you might find useful.

  • SAP partners and customers can join the SAP Asset Performance Management - Product Expert Training H2 2026 live session. Find details and register here. We're going to give a glimpse of the new AI agents coming out this year and the outlook for next year. 
  • We've also updated our ongoing innovation overview (formerly Stay Current), a curated guide to recent SAP APM innovations combining feature one-pagers with direct links to supporting enablement materials. The latest edition now covers releases 2509 - 2608. Download it here.

Now, let's take a closer look at SAP APM 2609.

Asset Reliability Engineering

5 Whys Root Cause Analysis in Reliability Cases

What if you could perform a structured root cause analysis directly inside SAP APM - without switching to a spreadsheet, a whiteboard, or a separate tool?

With this release, a dedicated 5 Whys root cause analysis section is now available inside Reliability Cases in SAP APM.

Challenge

When an asset failure occurs, reliability engineers need a structured methodology to trace the cause chain back to the origin. Until now, SAP APM had no built-in way to capture that analysis. Teams were working around the system - using external tools, documents, or informal notes - and the connection between root cause findings and follow-up actions was easily lost.

Solution

A dedicated 5 Whys analysis section is now part of the Reliability Case in SAP APM. Engineers can open a case, add cause chain levels one by one, and record the root cause with supporting context. The structured approach guides the team through the methodology while keeping all analysis and actions together in one place.

Because the analysis sits inside the Reliability Case, preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause. The completed analysis becomes part of the auditable case record - reusable for future investigations and visible to anyone who needs to understand how a failure was resolved.

5 Whys root cause analysis in SAP APM showing a completed cause chain for an unplanned gas turbine trip, with two converging fault branches traced from the problem through to root cause, and five corrective actions linked on the right.

Key Details

  • 5 Whys analysis section available inside Reliability Cases
  • Engineers add cause chain levels sequentially and record the root cause with context
  • Preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause
  • Analysis becomes part of the auditable Reliability Case record

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Root cause analysis completed entirely within SAP APM - no switching to external tools
  • Structured cause chains that are auditable and reusable for future failure investigations
  • Direct connection from root cause to preventive and corrective measures - nothing gets lost

Watch this video to see it in action

 

For more information, check this blog SAP Asset Performance Management Reliability Cases: A Practical Walkthrough Of Root Cause Analysis by @Pardhasaradhi_Reddy_Chelikam and see the SAP Help Portal Performing Root Cause Analysis.

Asset Health Monitoring

IoT Sensor Data Available in APM Within 15 Minutes

What if condition-based maintenance decisions were based on sensor readings from the last 15 minutes - not from two hours ago?

With this release, time series data ingested via the embedded IoT platform is now available in SAP APM rules and charts within 15 minutes of ingestion.

Challenge

Time series data sent from sensors into the embedded IoT platform could take up to two hours to appear in SAP APM. For teams using IoT data to drive condition-based maintenance rules and alerts, that delay meant rules fired late and the data behind a triggered alert was already stale. In fast-moving asset conditions, the gap between sensor reading and APM response was a real operational risk.

Solution

The data offloading interval and processing pipeline between the Embedded IoT platform and SAP APM has been significantly shortened. Time series data sent through standard HTTP and MQTT interfaces is now processed and made available in APM rules and the APM Chart within 15 minutes of ingestion - down from the previous baseline of up to 120 minutes.

No changes are required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations. Aggregate and analytics data sources are outside the scope of this improvement and may have longer processing times.

Key Details

  • Time series data via HTTP and MQTT available in APM within 15 minutes of ingestion
  • Applies to APM rules and the APM Chart
  • No changes required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations
  • Aggregate and analytics data sources are out of scope and may have longer processing times

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Near-current sensor data in APM rules and charts - processing time reduced from up to 120 minutes to 15 minutes
  • Condition-based maintenance scenarios trigger faster, reducing response time to developing asset issues
  • Improved reliability of IoT-driven alerting with fresher data as the foundation

entry.title: FSA Integration - How to Enable Parallel Processing in SAP Data Replication Framework (DRF)
entry.content:
Introduction

Replicating large amount of master data  from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Field Service and Asset Management (FSA) can take a very long time. If the system sends the data one by one, it creates a traffic jam that slows down your business.
The Data Replication Framework (DRF) Parallel Processing feature fixes this problem. Instead of sending everything in a single line, it chops the data into smaller chunks and sends them all at the exact same time. In this blog, I will explain how this process works using Equipment Replication as our example, and show you how to turn it on in your system.

DRF configuration

1.Business system and replication model: In transaction DRFIMG, maintain the business system under Define Technical Settings for Business Systems. Then create the replication model under Define Replication Model.

     

2. Outbound implementation: Assign the equipment outbound implementation (<your outbound implementation>) and the target business system to the replication model

3.Parameter values: On the outbound implementation assignment, maintain below parameter with Values.

Parameter

Purpose

TASK_SIZE_PROCMSG

Number of messages handled by one parallel task

PACK_SIZE_BULK

Number of objects packed into one bulk message call

PARALLEL_PROCESS_NEW

Enable Parallel processing

4.Run with parallel processing: In DRFOUT, select the replication model and the parallel processing checkbox, then execute or schedule it as a background job.

How DRF Parallel processes work with 100K equipment:

The settings used in this example are:

Item

Value

Result

Total messages

1,00,000

Equipment to process

TASK_SIZE_PROCMSG

1000

⌈100,000 / 1000⌉ = 100 parallel tasks

PACK_SIZE_BULK

100

10 Send_message calls per task, 1,000 in total

Free work processes

10

Only 10 tasks run at the same time

Rounds

⌈100 / 10⌉

10 rounds

Only the execution changes. The 100 tasks are pipelined across the 10 work processes:

Round 1:  Tasks   1– 10 run in parallel (Equipment      1 –  10,000)

Round 2:  Tasks  11– 20 run in parallel (Equipment 10,001 –  20,000)

……

…….

…….

Round 10: Tasks  91–100 run in parallel (Equipment 90,001 – 100,000)

Each work processes about 10 tasks one after another:

WP-1:  [Task 1] → [Task 11] → [Task 21] → ... → [Task 91]

WP-2:  [Task 2] → [Task 12] → [Task 22] → ... → [Task 92]

...

WP-10: [Task 10] → [Task 20] → [Task 30] → ... → [Task 100]

Conclusion:

With 100,000 equipment, a task size of 1000, and a bulk size of 100, DRF creates 100 tasks that send 10 bulk calls each. With only 10 free work processes, the tasks run in 10 rounds instead of a single parallel round. The work processes limit the elapsed time, not the task and bulk settings. If you can’t get more work processes, a larger task size reduces the task count but doesn’t speed up the run once all 10 work processes are busy. Fewer, larger tasks can even leave work processes idle at the end of the run. Size the task so that the number of tasks is a multiple of the free work processes and tune the bulk size against the target system’s limits.

 Please share your experiences in the comments.
